profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle, a two-part data center campus in Tukwila, King County, Washington, marketed by the operator as the West Coast's largest privately owned data center campus. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in this same Tukwila location became SDC Seattle Building 5, prompting Sabey's pivot into the data center industry. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia. As of 2026 Sabey operates seven data center campuses nationally, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet and, per Wikipedia's most recent figure, nearly 400 MW of capacity; Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood.

Per the operator's own SDC Seattle page, the Tukwila campus totals more than a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus-wide, a figure not broken out per individual building and not applied to any single structure here. Aggregator sourcing indicates the campus actually comprises two separately addressed sub-campuses: Intergate.East, at a street range of 3311 to 3511 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA 98168, spanning roughly 1.2 million square feet; and Intergate.West, at 12101 to 12301 Tukwila International Boulevard, Tukwila, WA 98168, built in 1999 and spanning roughly 173,000 square feet.

This building, Intergate.East Building 4, was previously misidentified in this registry as a Digital Realty facility. A DatacenterHawk listing titled "Sabey Data Centers Intergate.East Building 4," an exact match to this building's own designation, together with independently agreeing PeeringDB and DataCenterJournal listings, confirms Sabey as the current operator at 3433 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA. No record of a Digital Realty acquisition of this specific Sabey campus was found; the operator field on this row was corrected accordingly, with Digital Realty preserved as a former operator of record rather than deleted, since Intergate is Sabey's own registered campus brand and Digital Realty's own confirmed Seattle-area facility is separately branded SEA1.

profile.research_note: Gap-view review: Sabey publishes SDC Seattle only as a campus-wide total (1M+ sqft / 54MW across Intergate.East + Intergate.West sub-campuses), not broken out per building. No per-building figure exists for Intergate.East Building 4. No numeric key written.

profile.facility_type_note: The Westin Building at 2001 Sixth Avenue, downtown Seattle (Digital Realty's SEA10), is one of the most important internet exchange and carrier hotel buildings on the US West Coast, historically known as the Westin Building Exchange. Digital Realty acquired a controlling stake in the building, per Data Center Frontier and Commercial Property Executive coverage of the transaction. The Intergate facility in Tukwila is a separate building from the downtown Westin Building; Digital Realty also operates a facility (SEA1) at 3433 S 120th Place in the Seattle/Tukwila area per datacenterHawk.

reading.body:
Sabey Data Centers operates SDC Seattle in Tukwila, a two-building campus spanning roughly 1.4 million square feet across Intergate.East and Intergate.West. The operator publishes 54 MW of total campus capacity without breaking it out per building; no individual IT load figure for Building 4 is confirmed from a tier-1 source. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 54 MW would support roughly 1,350 racks, though this figure applies to the entire campus and the split between buildings is not published.

This campus ranks third by published capacity in Washington State, behind only two other facilities with disclosed megawattage in a state where 46 data centers are mapped but most publish no specification. The Tukwila location sits in the greater Seattle metro region on the U.S. West Coast, historically a carrier hotel and internet exchange hub, though the specific certifications and tenant categories this building qualifies to host are not published.

The campus capacity figure is not confirmed from independent infrastructure audit, and the distribution of the 54 MW across the two sub-campuses and four buildings in the Intergate.East group is not disclosed. Whether this facility has been upgraded or expanded since the operator's last published figure, or whether power supply at this location is constrained by local grid connection or other factors, is not stated in available sources.
